confirm.closeYearBody: The closing journal is posted, every profit and loss account is zeroed into retained earnings, and the year is marked closed. This is the last accounting action of the year.
confirm.unlockBody: It goes back to open and accepts ordinary journals again. Say why — the reason is kept on the record.

openingBalance.scopeBody: Bring in what clients and suppliers still owe first, with the client and supplier import (Excel) under Get started. Then post the trial balance here: its receivables and payables lines must equal those open documents, so the ledger and the documents agree from day one. Once the trial balance is posted, opening documents can no longer be imported.

create.accountHint: Active posting accounts in income, cost of sales and expenses.
create.noAccounts: The chart has no active posting account in income, cost of sales or expenses to point a profile at.

problem.name: Enter a name.
problem.code: Use capital letters, digits and underscores only (up to 50).
problem.code-taken: A posting profile with this code already exists.
problem.account: Choose the account the profile posts to.

create.accountInvalid: That account cannot take a posting profile. Choose an active posting account in income, cost of sales or expenses.

repoint.title: Re-point {code}
repoint.history: History is kept. Documents dated before the effective date stay on the current account; from that date on, postings go to the new one.

problem.same-account: The profile already posts to this account.
problem.effective-from: Choose the date the change takes effect.
problem.effective-from-early: The change must start after the current version, which starts on {date}.
problem.class-change: {family, select, REVENUE {This profile posts to income, so it can only be re-pointed to another income account.} other {This profile posts to cost of sales or expenses, so it can only be re-pointed to a cost-of-sales or expense account.}}

repoint.untilDay: The current account stays in force until {date}.
repoint.familyHint: {family, select, REVENUE {Income accounts only — a revenue profile stays a revenue profile.} other {Cost-of-sales and expense accounts only — a cost profile stays a cost profile.}}
repoint.changed: Someone changed this profile meanwhile. It has been reloaded — check it and try again.

deactivate.title: Deactivate {code}
deactivate.body: New bill lines can no longer choose it. Documents already posted with it are unchanged.
deactivate.inUse: {count, plural, one {# unposted supplier bill still uses this profile.} other {# unposted supplier bills still use this profile.}} Post or change them first.

reactivate.title: Reactivate {code}
reactivate.body: Bill lines can choose it again.

invoiceNumbering.title: Invoice numbering
invoiceNumbering.nextInvalid: Enter a whole number of 1 or more.
invoiceNumbering.dateNote: The date in the number is the invoice date, and the count starts again at 1 each period.
invoiceNumbering.saveFailed: Could not save the invoice numbering.
invoiceNumbering.loadFailed: Could not load the invoice numbering.

invoiceSettings.title: Invoice settings
invoiceSettings.description: What every client invoice PDF prints besides the invoice itself: the tagline, the footer contacts, the authorised signatory, and the optional bank details and notes.
invoiceSettings.frozenNotice: Invoices take these settings when they are raised and again when they are issued. A PDF already generated never changes.
invoiceSettings.readOnly: Only Finance (manage accounting) can change these settings.
invoiceSettings.loadFailed: Could not load the invoice settings.
invoiceSettings.saveFailed: Could not save the invoice settings.
invoiceSettings.banksHint: A table of bank and account number, in this order, with the invoice number as the payment reference.
invoiceSettings.maxBanks: An invoice prints at most {max} bank accounts.
invoiceSettings.rowIncomplete: Each bank needs both a bank name and an account number.
invoiceSettings.signatoryHint: Printed under the signature line. Left blank, invoices show an empty signature line.
invoiceSettings.notesHint: One note per line; they print as a numbered list.
invoiceSettings.defaultsApply: Left blank, invoices print the standard notes:
invoiceSettings.headerHint: Printed under the logo (or the company name when there is no logo), in small spaced capitals.
invoiceSettings.footerHint: The strip along the bottom of every page: address, phone numbers, email and website. Empty fields are left out.
invoiceSettings.footerAddressPlaceholder: e.g. Olow Tower, Maka Al-Mukarama Road
invoiceSettings.footerAddressDefault: Left blank, the footer prints the organisation address shown above.
invoiceSettings.emailInvalid: Enter an email address like info@company.com.
invoiceSettings.showBankDetails: Print bank account details on invoices
invoiceSettings.showBankDetailsHint: Off by default: the minimal invoice has no bank section.
invoiceSettings.showNotesHint: Off by default: the minimal invoice has no notes.
invoiceSettings.footerAddressHint: Up to {lines} lines of {chars} characters each.
invoiceSettings.footerAddressInvalid: The footer fits 2 lines of 60 characters each. Shorten the address.
invoiceSettings.previewHint: The real PDF with your current settings, updated as you type. The client, project and amounts are a sample.
invoiceSettings.previewFailed: The preview could not be rendered.
invoiceSettings.previewPartial: Some values are not complete yet and are left out of the preview until they are.

approvalSettings.title: Approval rules
approvalSettings.description: Which finance documents need a second person before they reach the ledger. Everything else is approved as it is saved. Changes apply to documents saved from now on.
approvalSettings.readOnly: Only someone who manages accounting can change these rules.
approvalSettings.loadFailed: The approval rules could not be loaded.
approvalSettings.invoicesDescription: Issue numbers an invoice and posts it in one step.
approvalSettings.invoiceSwitch: Large invoices need approval before they are issued
approvalSettings.invoiceSwitchHint: Someone other than the person who prepared it approves it from Approvals.
approvalSettings.invoiceAbove: Invoices of this amount or more
approvalSettings.billsDescription: A bill that passes these rules posts as soon as it is saved.
approvalSettings.billSwitch: Large bills without a purchase order need approval
approvalSettings.billSwitchHint: Bills against a purchase order are checked by the three-way match instead.
approvalSettings.billAbove: Bills of this amount or more
approvalSettings.toleratedSwitch: Post bills that match their purchase order within tolerance
approvalSettings.toleratedHint: Off: only an exact match posts on save; a tolerated difference waits for approval.
approvalSettings.paymentsDescription: Bank signatory release and the approval bands above this limit always apply. Client refunds and transfers between your own accounts follow the same limit: above it, a second person approves.
approvalSettings.paymentSwitch: Approve small payments as they are saved
approvalSettings.paymentSwitchHint: A payment that settles a bill the same person approved still needs someone else.
approvalSettings.amountInvalid: Enter an amount with at most two decimals.
approvalSettings.saveFailed: The approval rules could not be saved.
approvalSettings.writeOffsDescription: A balance a client will not pay is written off to Bad debts. Small ones post at once; larger ones are approved by a second person.
approvalSettings.writeOffAboveHint: Enter 0 to send every write-off for approval.

statement.title: Client statement
statement.pickBody: See what the client owes on each project and contract, which invoices are unpaid, and every payment.
statement.loadFailed: The statement could not be loaded.
statement.nothingInPeriod: Nothing was charged, paid or credited in this period.
statement.agingTitle: Open invoices today, by days past due
statement.noAccounts: Nothing has been billed to this client yet.
statement.nothingOwed: Nothing is owed: every invoice is paid.
statement.daysOverdue: {count, plural, one {# day overdue} other {# days overdue}}
statement.periodLine: {from} to {to}: opened at {opening}, charged {charged}, paid and credited {paid}, closed at {closing}.
statement.pdfFailed: The statement PDF could not be made. Try again.
statement.whatsappSubtitle: The statement for {client} as of {date} goes to the client as a PDF.

writeOff.title: Write off a balance
writeOff.heading: Write-offs

reasonHint.SMALL_BALANCE: A leftover not worth collecting — bank charges, rounding.
reasonHint.BAD_DEBT: The client will not pay: insolvent, disputed beyond recovery, or untraceable.

writeOff.reasonRequired: Choose why it is written off.
writeOff.amountRequired: Enter an amount greater than zero.
writeOff.amountOverBalance: This is more than the invoice still owes.
writeOff.postsNow: It posts now: the amount moves to Bad debts and the invoice owes that much less.
writeOff.approvalBody: Write-offs above {limit} are approved by someone else before they post.
writeOff.failed: That did not go through. Try again.
writeOff.rejectBody: The balance stays on the invoice. Say why, so the person who asked knows what to do next.
writeOff.reverseBody: Use this when the client pays after all. A reversing entry is posted today and the invoice owes the amount again.

supplierStatement.title: Supplier statement
supplierStatement.subtitle: Everything a supplier billed and was paid in a period, with what is owed — to agree with the statement they send.
supplierStatement.pickBody: The statement lists every bill and payment for the supplier across all projects, with a running balance of what is owed.
supplierStatement.loadFailed: The statement could not be loaded.
supplierStatement.unapplied: {amount} paid ahead, not yet applied to a bill
supplierStatement.nothingInPeriod: Nothing was billed or paid in this period.
supplierStatement.agingTitle: Open bills today, by days past due
supplierStatement.pdfFailed: The PDF could not be made. Try again.
supplierStatement.openNone: Nothing is owed: every bill is paid.
supplierStatement.daysLate: {days, plural, one {# day late} other {# days late}}
supplierStatement.whatsappSubtitle: Our record of {supplier} up to {date} goes as a PDF, so they can check it against theirs.

tieOut.title: AR/AP tie-out
tieOut.noControls: No receivable or payable control account in the chart.
tieOut.differsTitle: The books and the documents disagree
tieOut.differsBody: Something posted to a control account without an invoice or bill, or a document changed without posting. The month cannot close until they agree.
